text:
alicia: quick proposal — automatic "spill" to compatible variants when a primary model is saturated. goal: keep latency SLOs without manual runbook swaps. thinking default behavior: region-local compatible variant -> tier-aware preference -> quantized variant fallback. thoughts?

sam: spicy. how do we bill/attribute tokens if we spill? tenants will freak if usage jumps on a cheaper quantized model vs primary. need deterministic telemetry. :grimacing:

marta: we can add an API header to control preference: `X-Redwood-Prefer-Primary: true|false|prefer` and emit `meta.variant_used` in responses + per-request telemetry tags. billing would attribute to the variant actually served.

kevin: also need to consider cold-starts for the backup variant. if we spill and it’s not warm, we might blow latency. propose a soft-spill where router probes capacity and, if cold, enqueues a warmup or routes to regional compatible model. maybe pre-warm for high-tier customers.

priya: console UX idea: each model in the rollout page shows a "spill threshold" slider (percent of saturation) and a "force primary" toggle for legal/SLA customers. as part of the rollout you can stage spill policy: dry-run -> telemetry-only -> active.

ops-bot: alert: primary-model=gptx-8k-1 saturated in us-east-1 (util 98%); auto-spill triggered to gptx-8k-q4_us-east. sample payload: `{\"tenant\":\"acme\",\"req_id\":\"f3e2\"}`

marta: +1 to emitting `primary_unavailable_reason` in response meta (overloaded|capacity|maintenance) so SDKs can surface and customers can optionally retry or fall back locally. also add a telemetry counter: `router.spill.count` and `router.spill.latency.p50/95`.

sam: API-level debate: do we return 200 with meta about variant used, or surface a 503 when primary not used? my vote: always 200 if we can serve (but include `meta.primary_was_targeted: true/false`). 503 only when nothing compatible available.

kevin: policy defaults: enterprise tier -> try primary up to 750ms, then allow up to 20% of requests to be forced to primary (try harder), otherwise spill; free tier -> immediate spill preference to cheaper/quantized variants. default policies should be overridable per-tenant.

alicia: ok actionable list: 1) API header + response meta spec (marta lead) 2) telemetry counters and console charts (priya lead) 3) default tier policies + pre-warm heuristic (kevin lead) 4) billing attribution doc (sam lead). I'll open a PR with the rough schema and console mockups. thanks everyone — if you want to opt-out of auto-spill for a tenant, add `X-Redwood-Prefer-Primary: true` for now. :white_check_mark:
